formula: Subject + replied / answered / argued, “That may be so, but + clause.”

formulas.formula: Subject + replied / answered / argued, “That may be so, but + clause.”

example: That may be so, but it does not solve the immediate problem.
exampleZh: 話雖如此，但這並不能解決眼前的問題。

examples.en: That may be so, but it does not solve the immediate problem.
examples.zh: 話雖如此，但這並不能解決眼前的問題。
examples.highlight: That may be so, but it does not solve the immediate problem.

rules.zh: 這裏的【that】並非指某一件物件，而是代表前面提出的整個意見、聲稱或論點。例如，公司表示這套系統很安全；話雖如此，仍有需要進一步測試。詞語【That】代表前文所說的整項內容。
rules.en: That The company says the system is safe. That may be so, but further testing is necessary. the system is safe

rules.zh: 目標表達【may】表示有限度的承認目標表達【That may be so】並不等於：【That is definitely true.】 那肯定是真的。 它比較接近：【I accept that what you said may be true.】 我承認你所說的可能是真的。 因此，這個句型可以讓說話者表現得較為公平，同時保留不同意見。
rules.en: may That may be so That is definitely true. I accept that what you said may be true.

rules.zh: 後面必須有完整意思不完整：【That may be so, but the cost.】 話雖如此，但成本。 完整：【That may be so, but the cost is still too high.】 話雖如此，但成本仍然太高。 本練習要求 but 後面使用完整子句。
rules.en: but That may be so, but the cost. That may be so, but the cost is still too high.

rules.zh: 轉折詞 but 和 however 不可在同一位置重複使用。可寫 That may be so, but...，或另起一句用 However,...。
rules.en: That may be so, but however, we need more evidence. That may be so, but we need more evidence. That may be so. However, we need more evidence.

rules.zh: 前面的說法必須清楚不清楚：【That may be so, but we cannot agree.】 讀者不知道 that 代表甚麼。較清楚：【You say the change will save money. That may be so, but we cannot agree to the safety risks.】 你說這項改變可以節省金錢。話雖如此，但我們不能接受相關的安全風險。
rules.en: That may be so, but we cannot agree. You say the change will save money. That may be so, but we cannot agree to the safety risks.

rules.zh: 這個句型主要用於有真正反差的情況不自然：【The shop is open. That may be so, but customers can enter.】 前後兩項內容並沒有真正的反差。自然：【The shop is open. That may be so, but most of its products are unavailable.】 商店正在營業。話雖如此，但大部分貨品都沒有供應。
rules.en: The shop is open. That may be so, but customers can enter. That may be so, but most of its products are unavailable.

rules.zh: 本練習要求使用完整固定形式本練習的目標是：【That may be so, but + clause】 以下相關形式雖然可能正確，但不屬於本課的指定答案：【That might be so, but...；That may well be so, but...；This may be true, but...；Even so,...；Granted,...】
rules.en: That may be so, but + clause That might be so, but... That may well be so, but... This may be true, but... Even so,... Granted,...

benefits.zh: 幫助你有禮貌地提出不同意見你不需要立即指出對方錯誤，而是先承認對方的說法可能有道理，再提出自己的意見。你錯了。這個計劃風險太高。 話雖如此，但這個計劃的風險仍然太高。 第二種說法通常較為平衡，也較適合討論、會議和正式寫作。
benefits.en: It helps you disagree politely Instead of immediately saying that another person is wrong, you first acknowledge that the person may have a reasonable point. Compare: You are wrong. The plan is too risky. That may be so, but the plan is still too risky.

benefits.zh: 表示你有考慮雙方觀點這個句型表示你有聆聽和考慮對方的論點，而不是直接忽視不同意見。
benefits.en: It shows that you have considered both sides This structure shows that you have listened to the other person instead of simply ignoring the opposing argument.

benefits.zh: 讓主要反駁保持清楚在【but】後面的內容是說話者真正想強調的重點，因此讀者可以清楚知道哪一項意見較為重要。
benefits.en: It keeps the main counterpoint clear The words after but contain the speaker’s main message. The reader can therefore understand which point is more important.

benefits.zh: 令論述顯得更平衡在作文、討論和簡報中，較有說服力的論述通常會先承認一項可能的優點，再解釋一個更加嚴重的問題。這項建議可能創造職位。話雖如此，但它對環境造成的破壞可能是永久的。
benefits.en: It makes arguments sound more balanced In essays, discussions and presentations, strong arguments often acknowledge a possible advantage before explaining a more serious problem. The proposal may create jobs. That may be so, but the environmental damage could be permanent.

benefits.zh: 提供一個容易使用的口語框架說話時，你可以先使用這個固定開首，讓自己有時間整理接下來的反駁。這個框架適合用於：小組討論辯論會議口試日常意見交流
benefits.en: It gives you a ready-made speaking frame When speaking, you can use the fixed opening to give yourself time to organise the counterpoint. That may be so, but...

benefits.zh: 避免過度重複 although 或 however 你不需要每次都使用 although 或 however 表達反差。當你回應另一項說法時，可以使用這個句型增加句式變化。
benefits.en: It provides an alternative to overusing although or however Instead of beginning every contrast with although or however, you can use this structure as a direct response to another claim.
